statusDetail: Coverage-complete model-driven audit of representative homepage, article, listing, search, error, and account-entry surfaces.

page.notes: Public multilingual FIFA content portal. Core routes render from an empty #root shell; no local source was supplied.

checkOutcomes.method: evaluate computed styles plus dark-media screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: Computed-style probe reports color-scheme: normal, and the dark-emulated capture retains the same hard-coded palette rather than declaring a user-preference-driven scheme.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the page still runs a 10.5 s hero animation and more than 100 repeating 1 s skeleton animations; the probe found zero reduced-motion CSS rules.
The forced-colors/prefers-contrast capture preserves visible text, controls, outlines, and consent actions.
Computed styles expose view-transition-name: root and the recorded search route change provides direct transition evidence.
DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll-timeline rules and the reviewed pages did not present parallax or scrollytelling that would require a scroll-linked implementation.
The homepage contains carousel-style content but computed-style inspection found no scroll-snap or overscroll treatment on any element, so gesture behavior is not platform-native.
Computed styles identify the primary header as position: sticky at top: 0, keeping navigation available as content scrolls.
The representative pages exposed full-screen search/consent dialogs but no tooltip or edge-attached popover whose position needed CSS anchor positioning.
checkOutcomes.reason: The representative pages exposed full-screen search/consent dialogs but no tooltip or edge-attached popover whose position needed CSS anchor positioning.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Opening the search route moves focus directly to the search input, and the overlay visibly separates the active task from the underlying page.
The first viewport is simultaneously obscured by a centered Play Zone promotion and a large consent wall; on mobile the consent wall occupies essentially the entire viewport.
The consent and privacy overlays are DIV elements with role=dialog; the primary banner lacks aria-modal and the search overlay is custom rather than a native dialog/popover.
Two stacked overlays plus two navigation bars leave the actual football content dimmed and largely unavailable in the initial viewport.
At 360x800 the layout primitive reports scrollWidth=clientWidth=360, zero horizontal overflow, and a viewport meta tag.
CSSOM inspection found 16 container rules, and the tested homepage/article/category surfaces reflowed to the 360 px viewport without overflow.
Keyboard focus probes show visible outlines on navigation, search, account, consent, and menu controls; the mobile target inventory found only two text controls below 24 px high.
The homepage H1 and dominant action describe Play Zone rather than the FIFA news/content destination, while promotional and consent overlays compete for the first action.
The representative discovery flow completes from homepage links to a fully rendered article, and the search route opens with focus in the query field.

checkOutcomes.method: HTTP probe, DOM probe, and screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: A nonexistent route returns HTTP 200, has an empty title, and shows only a joke message with no home, search, back, or retry link.
Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 29.3 s and TBT 1,860 ms; the article measured LCP 33.8 s, TBT 1,990 ms, and CLS 1.108. A separate trace measured LCP 5.84 s.
The article Lighthouse run measured CLS 1.108, and the mobile layout observer recorded CLS 1.35 with two approximately 0.61 shifts after load.
The trace recorded four long tasks, a 355 ms longest task, and 375 ms total blocking time; Lighthouse measured 1.86-1.99 s TBT.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary plus script attribute probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The HAR records 6.0 MB over 87 requests, 4.07 MB of script, eight fonts, missing cache headers on a 1.77 MB auth SDK, and multiple synchronous parser-inserted head scripts confirmed by DOM inspection.
The homepage ships 35 scripts totaling 4.07 MB; a 1.77 MB PingOne SDK, 783 KB consent blocker, 325 KB PDF worker, and other integrations load before the user requests those capabilities.
Lighthouse found aria-prohibited-attr and label-content-name-mismatch on the homepage and an unnamed button on the article.
Lighthouse color-contrast audits fail on both the homepage and article despite forced-colors remaining usable.
Lighthouse reports heading-order failure on the homepage; the DOM starts at H1 then repeated H3 cards and injects extensive consent-dialog headings into document structure.
Article screenshots show readable line length, clear hierarchy, and no clipped body text at desktop and mobile widths.
Viewport content allows scaling, 360 px layouts have no horizontal overflow, focus remains visible, and the target probe found the primary controls appropriately sized.
Lighthouse reports errors-in-console on both the homepage and article.
The document has valid HTML doctype/UTF-8, but the image audit found two images without intrinsic dimensions and one asset rendered from a source more than 15x wider than display size.
Lighthouse reports invalid source maps on both templates and a BFCache failure on the homepage.
Rendered homepage and article each have descriptive, route-specific titles and meta descriptions.
Lighthouse reports non-descriptive link text on both pages and non-crawlable anchors on the article, even though viewport and robots basics are present.

checkOutcomes.method: metadata, Lighthouse, robots/sitemap, and HTTP probes
checkOutcomes.evidence: The article exposes no canonical link, its og:url incorrectly points to /fifaplus, Lighthouse flags hreflang, and nonexistent routes return HTTP 200.
The news article has no JSON-LD structured data and its Open Graph URL is https://www.fifa.com/fifaplus rather than the visible article URL.
HTTPS, HSTS and nosniff are present, but CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval and the bm_sz cookie is not Secure with SameSite=None.

checkOutcomes.method: consent screenshot, HAR, and tracker audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: The consent wall names 1,017 partners; the HAR records 47 third-party requests transferring 4.11 MB and the tracker inventory finds 12 third-party origins.

Notification/geolocation remain prompt rather than being requested on load, but the account/auth surface exposed no passkey or WebAuthn flow and the inspected /auth route produced an empty-title dead end.
HSTS, SAMEORIGIN, no-referrer and nosniff are configured, but Permissions-Policy is missing and the CSP relies on unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval with an exceptionally broad allowlist.
Raw HTML for homepage, category and article is an empty #root shell: 0% rendered content coverage, no raw title/H1/description, and blank crawler screenshots without JavaScript.
Search remains focused and usable as a full-width overlay, while inspected sticky navigation stays within the viewport and no clipped edge menus appeared on tested paths.
A standalone web app manifest exists, but navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations() returned no registrations, so no offline fallback is active.
The tested missing route returns a soft-404 HTTP 200 and offers no actionable recovery control, title, or link.
The page declares lang=en and dir=ltr and exposes ten localized hreflang variants; alternate-language URLs are present for the article.
The article renders a localized human-readable publication date and supplies distinct language-specific article URLs for ten locales.
The representative news, listing, search, and error surfaces exposed no event times, scheduling, recurrence, or cross-time-zone interaction to evaluate.
checkOutcomes.reason: The representative news, listing, search, and error surfaces exposed no event times, scheduling, recurrence, or cross-time-zone interaction to evaluate.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The consent wall presents I Accept and Reject All as equally prominent controls and states the consequences of each choice; no preselected purchase or forced-continuity flow was observed.
The exercised first-party surfaces contained search but no required-input form or validation flow; article, listing, and search navigation did not solicit error-prone user data.
checkOutcomes.reason: The exercised first-party surfaces contained search but no required-input form or validation flow; article, listing, and search navigation did not solicit error-prone user data.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The only first-party text input exercised was site search, which does not require address, payment, sign-in, or sign-up autofill tokens.
checkOutcomes.reason: The only first-party text input exercised was site search, which does not require address, payment, sign-in, or sign-up autofill tokens.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Store, ticketing, rewards and Play Zone are separate linked products; no checkout, subscription, cancellation, or account-management flow was available within the audited fifa.com templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: Store, ticketing, rewards and Play Zone are separate linked products; no checkout, subscription, cancellation, or account-management flow was available within the audited fifa.com templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The page transfers 437 KB of images and the image audit finds an oversized logo source (1178 px natural width for 74 px display) plus a legacy PNG.

The initial load fetches a PDF worker, a 1.77 MB auth SDK, consent/analytics integrations, and 35 scripts before those capabilities are requested, while trace/Lighthouse show substantial blocking work.
Third parties account for 47 requests and 4.11 MB, about 69% of transferred bytes; PingOne and OneTrust alone transfer roughly 2.87 MB.
This globally prominent content site exposes no WebMCP/agentic form capability, while non-JavaScript agents receive an empty shell with 0% content coverage.
The audited content, listing, search, and navigation tasks do not require on-device generation or summarisation; no user-facing inference feature was present.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited content, listing, search, and navigation tasks do not require on-device generation or summarisation; no user-facing inference feature was present.

checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten repeated search-input updates, retained snapshot totals decreased slightly: nodes 1,491,962 to 1,491,952 and self size 80,838,979 to 80,804,689 bytes.
A single homepage/search state retains about 80.8 MB across 1.49 million heap nodes, a large footprint for a content/search page before extended use.
The repeated-interaction snapshot did not grow overall nodes, edges, closures, Objects, or Arrays, and no Detached constructor appeared among size-leading constructors.

paths.description: Homepage and global navigation, representative landing/content-discovery template; tested desktop, mobile, dark, reduced-motion, high-contrast, performance, privacy, security, network, and memory conditions.
Current World Cup awards article, representative long-form editorial/detail template and primary homepage destination.
Top stories category, representative listing/index template.
Search overlay and repeated-query interaction, representative first-party interactive flow.
Nonexistent content route, representative HTTP/runtime failure and recovery state.
Account-entry/auth route reached from the global account affordance, used to inspect permission/auth posture.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-color-scheme: a usable dark mode exists and is driven by the user's preference (color-scheme / prefers-color-scheme / light-dark()), not hard-coded light only.
findings.evidence: Computed-style probe reports color-scheme: normal, and the dark-emulated capture retains the same hard-coded palette rather than declaring a user-preference-driven scheme.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and map surfaces/text to preference-aware tokens such as light-dark().

findings.summary: Honours prefers-reduced-motion: non-essential animations and auto-advance are reduced or removed when the user asks for less motion.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the page still runs a 10.5 s hero animation and more than 100 repeating 1 s skeleton animations; the probe found zero reduced-motion CSS rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce branch that disables auto-advance and non-essential hero/skeleton animation.

findings.summary: Gesture-driven interactions and entry/exit motion feel native (declarative overscroll/scroll-snap, physics-based easing, animating to intrinsic sizes, pull/swipe gestures) rather than fighting the platform with custom pointer handlers.
findings.evidence: The homepage contains carousel-style content but computed-style inspection found no scroll-snap or overscroll treatment on any element, so gesture behavior is not platform-native.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native overflow with scroll-snap-type/scroll-snap-align and appropriate overscroll behavior for swipeable rails.

findings.summary: No intrusive pop-ups, interstitials or banners that obscure content on load; overlays are dismissible and content-first.
findings.evidence: The first viewport is simultaneously obscured by a centered Play Zone promotion and a large consent wall; on mobile the consent wall occupies essentially the entire viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not stack promotional and consent overlays; defer the Play Zone promotion and keep core content available.

findings.summary: Overlays and rich controls use the right primitive: popover (with declarative light-dismiss) for transient UI, dialog for modal flows, details for disclosure, native-but-branded selects and pickers, rather than ad-hoc divs.
findings.evidence: The consent and privacy overlays are DIV elements with role=dialog; the primary banner lacks aria-modal and the search overlay is custom rather than a native dialog/popover.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement modal flows with <dialog> and transient UI with popover, including native focus and light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Minimise non-content chrome and borders so the content is the focus, not the application frame; expressive/decorative visuals serve the content rather than crowd it.
findings.evidence: Two stacked overlays plus two navigation bars leave the actual football content dimmed and largely unavailable in the initial viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove competing initial chrome and reserve the first viewport for the page purpose and primary content.

findings.summary: The page communicates what it is for and exposes the primary next action without requiring users to hunt through decorative content, generic copy, or competing calls to action.
findings.evidence: The homepage H1 and dominant action describe Play Zone rather than the FIFA news/content destination, while promotional and consent overlays compete for the first action.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore a content-oriented H1 and one clear next action; present Play Zone as optional secondary promotion.

findings.summary: Loading, empty, success, error, offline, and partial-completion states are visible and actionable; users can retry, undo, cancel, go back, or continue without losing context.
findings.evidence: A nonexistent route returns HTTP 200, has an empty title, and shows only a joke message with no home, search, back, or retry link.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a real 404 and provide clear Home, Search, and Back recovery actions with a descriptive title.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are in the good range: LCP is fast, interaction latency (INP) is low, and CLS is minimal; work is prioritised and deferred sensibly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 29.3 s and TBT 1,860 ms; the article measured LCP 33.8 s, TBT 1,990 ms, and CLS 1.108. A separate trace measured LCP 5.84 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a performance budget and prioritize the LCP path; defer non-critical integrations until after content and interaction readiness.

findings.summary: No cumulative layout shift from late content (images, banners, fonts) that arrives without reserved space.
findings.evidence: The article Lighthouse run measured CLS 1.108, and the mobile layout observer recorded CLS 1.35 with two approximately 0.61 shifts after load.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for late sections/media and make overlays or dynamic content enter without moving existing content.

findings.summary: The main thread is not blocked by long tasks or heavy scripting; work is deferred, chunked, prioritised, or moved off-thread.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded four long tasks, a 355 ms longest task, and 375 ms total blocking time; Lighthouse measured 1.86-1.99 s TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up startup tasks, defer optional SDK initialization, and schedule non-critical work after the page becomes interactive.

findings.summary: Critical resources are delivered efficiently: cache headers are useful, render-blocking chains are short, fonts do not block or shift text, HTTP delivery is modern, and network dependency trees do not delay the main content.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 6.0 MB over 87 requests, 4.07 MB of script, eight fonts, missing cache headers on a 1.77 MB auth SDK, and multiple synchronous parser-inserted head scripts confirmed by DOM inspection.
findings.suggestedFix: Make non-critical scripts async/deferred or interaction-triggered, trim preloads, and add durable cache headers.

findings.summary: The page does not ship large unused or duplicated JavaScript/CSS, avoidable legacy bundles, or third-party code that dominates the load without user value.
findings.evidence: The homepage ships 35 scripts totaling 4.07 MB; a 1.77 MB PingOne SDK, 783 KB consent blocker, 325 KB PDF worker, and other integrations load before the user requests those capabilities.
findings.suggestedFix: Load auth, PDF, video, consent extensions, and analytics only on routes or interactions that need them.

findings.summary: Interactive elements have accessible names, correct roles, and form fields have labels; images have alt text where meaningful; canvas/expressive content is exposed to assistive technology.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found aria-prohibited-attr and label-content-name-mismatch on the homepage and an unnamed button on the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix Lighthouse ARIA/name failures and give every icon button a stable accessible name matching its visible label.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI meet WCAG colour-contrast minimums against their background.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast audits fail on both the homepage and article despite forced-colors remaining usable.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust failing foreground/background token pairs to meet WCAG AA in normal rendering.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is logical, focus order follows reading order, keyboard focus is always visible, and interactive state survives DOM moves.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports heading-order failure on the homepage; the DOM starts at H1 then repeated H3 cards and injects extensive consent-dialog headings into document structure.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sequential heading hierarchy and isolate consent-dialog headings from the underlying page structure.

findings.summary: The page loads without console errors or uncaught exceptions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports errors-in-console on both the homepage and article.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve runtime console exceptions on both templates and add smoke coverage that fails on uncaught errors.

findings.summary: Valid doctype and charset, images sized with correct aspect ratio, no deprecated APIs misused, and CSS/HTML are well structured and not needlessly repetitive. (HTTPS, CSP and permission hygiene are judged under be-private-and-secure, not here.)
findings.evidence: The document has valid HTML doctype/UTF-8, but the image audit found two images without intrinsic dimensions and one asset rendered from a source more than 15x wider than display size.
findings.suggestedFix: Give all images intrinsic dimensions and serve the logo at an appropriate responsive size.

findings.summary: The page uses the platform cleanly: no deprecated APIs, no avoidable BFCache blockers, no broken source maps or inspector issues, no stale vulnerable libraries, no paste-prevention on inputs, and no notification/geolocation prompts on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports invalid source maps on both templates and a BFCache failure on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish valid source maps for production diagnostics and remove the reported BFCache blockers.

findings.summary: Links are crawlable (real href), there is a viewport meta tag, robots does not block indexing, and link text is descriptive.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports non-descriptive link text on both pages and non-crawlable anchors on the article, even though viewport and robots basics are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Use descriptive link text and real href anchors for every navigational destination.

findings.summary: Public pages expose the indexing signals search engines need: successful HTTP status, canonical URL when appropriate, hreflang for localized variants, robots/sitemap consistency, and no accidental noindex/noarchive policy.
findings.evidence: The article exposes no canonical link, its og:url incorrectly points to /fifaplus, Lighthouse flags hreflang, and nonexistent routes return HTTP 200.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit correct per-route canonical/hreflang signals and real HTTP 404 status for missing routes.

findings.summary: Where the page represents an article, product, organization, event, place or other rich entity, structured data and share-preview metadata accurately describe the visible content.
findings.evidence: The news article has no JSON-LD structured data and its Open Graph URL is https://www.fifa.com/fifaplus rather than the visible article URL.
findings.suggestedFix: Add NewsArticle JSON-LD and set og:url to the canonical article URL.

findings.summary: Served over HTTPS with a sensible Content-Security-Policy and secure, SameSite cookies; no mixed content or obvious transport/header smells.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS and nosniff are present, but CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval and the bm_sz cookie is not Secure with SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Move to nonce/hash-based CSP without unsafe-eval and mark all transport-sensitive cookies Secure with an appropriate SameSite value.

findings.summary: No over-collection of user data, no leaky third parties, and analytics/background data collection is minimised and batched rather than chatty or session-wide by default.
findings.evidence: The consent wall names 1,017 partners; the HAR records 47 third-party requests transferring 4.11 MB and the tracker inventory finds 12 third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce partner scope and prevent optional analytics/ad/auth vendors from loading until purpose-specific consent and need.

findings.summary: Permission prompts are requested in context (not on load), and authentication uses modern, phishing-resistant methods (passkeys / WebAuthn) where relevant rather than passwords alone.
findings.evidence: Notification/geolocation remain prompt rather than being requested on load, but the account/auth surface exposed no passkey or WebAuthn flow and the inspected /auth route produced an empty-title dead end.
findings.suggestedFix: Make account entry reliable and offer discoverable WebAuthn/passkey authentication rather than an opaque SDK/dead route.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are configured where appropriate: HSTS, clickjacking protection (frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options), Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive apps, origin isolation, privacy-preserving third-party cookie posture, and sensible Referrer-Policy / Permissions-Policy.
findings.evidence: HSTS, SAMEORIGIN, no-referrer and nosniff are configured, but Permissions-Policy is missing and the CSP relies on unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval with an exceptionally broad allowlist.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy and tighten CSP source lists and script execution policy.

findings.summary: Core content and primary flows are reachable and usable without JavaScript and on older or non-Baseline browsers; modern features layer on as enhancements with fallbacks, and reactive/transition state stabilises rather than flickering before it settles.
findings.evidence: Raw HTML for homepage, category and article is an empty #root shell: 0% rendered content coverage, no raw title/H1/description, and blank crawler screenshots without JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render titles, headings, article/list content, and links so core content works without JavaScript; hydrate enhancements afterward.

findings.summary: Where the site is an app, it is installable (web app manifest) and offers an offline fallback and works on flaky networks. (Contextual: a brochure or intrinsically-online site may reasonably not need this.)
findings.evidence: A standalone web app manifest exists, but navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations() returned no registrations, so no offline fallback is active.
findings.suggestedFix: Either register a scoped service worker with a useful offline fallback or remove app-installability signals that imply offline resilience.

findings.summary: HTTP errors, network failures, timeouts and stale data states are handled intentionally: users see useful recovery options rather than blank screens, infinite spinners, broken shells, or misleading success states.
findings.evidence: The tested missing route returns a soft-404 HTTP 200 and offers no actionable recovery control, title, or link.
findings.suggestedFix: Return semantic error status and provide useful recovery navigation for failed routes and data loads.

findings.summary: Images and decorative assets are optimised and served at appropriate resolutions; decorative pseudo-element imagery and heavy decorative images are resolution-optimised rather than oversized.
findings.evidence: The page transfers 437 KB of images and the image audit finds an oversized logo source (1178 px natural width for 74 px display) plus a legacy PNG.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve appropriately sized AVIF/WebP responsive sources and avoid downloading oversized logo/decorative assets.

findings.summary: Background work and fetching are not wasteful: background processing is efficient and de-prioritised, and the lightest technique that achieves the result is preferred over heavy or redundant work.
findings.evidence: The initial load fetches a PDF worker, a 1.77 MB auth SDK, consent/analytics integrations, and 35 scripts before those capabilities are requested, while trace/Lighthouse show substantial blocking work.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally import route-specific SDKs and deprioritize analytics/background processing.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts, fonts, video, audio, animation and heavy media are proportionate to the user value they provide; autoplay or background media is avoided unless essential and resource use is cached or deferred where possible.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 47 requests and 4.11 MB, about 69% of transferred bytes; PingOne and OneTrust alone transfer roughly 2.87 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt a third-party byte/request budget and lazy-load optional vendors after interaction or consent.

findings.summary: Where it makes sense, the site exposes structured, safe capabilities to agents via WebMCP tools, agentic forms, and agentic JavaScript tools rather than leaving agents to scrape and guess.
findings.evidence: This globally prominent content site exposes no WebMCP/agentic form capability, while non-JavaScript agents receive an empty shell with 0% content coverage.
findings.suggestedFix: First make content server-readable, then expose safe structured search/content capabilities where WebMCP adds user value.

findings.summary: Heap size and DOM node count are reasonable for what the page is; the footprint is proportionate rather than bloated.
findings.evidence: A single homepage/search state retains about 80.8 MB across 1.49 million heap nodes, a large footprint for a content/search page before extended use.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce always-loaded SDKs and DOM/object populations, then set and monitor a retained-heap budget per template.

taskList.title: Server-render core content and route metadata
Stabilise layout and reserve late content space
Tighten privacy and browser security policy
Correct platform, image, and console hygiene
Make account entry reliable and modern
Use native gesture and optional agent capabilities
